issues.claim: §7.1's lock row (l. 10631) refuses `refuse.locked` a map event that 'crosses, targets or moves a locked or pinned entity — a drawn way across a locked entity'. Round 6's (D5) parenthesis exempts only work passing beneath a held raised way: 'never a ground way, a carve or a wall stretch passing beneath a locked or pinned raised way's deck, which changes none of its parts'. R6-02 made the reverse meeting write nothing too: an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall crosses it on a span over its band, 'nothing of the wall is written' (§2.7's crossing table, *over the band*, l. 2603), and by hand 'its dry run bends the course … (`bend.wall.aqueductArch`)' (l. 2691–2692). §7.1's *Raised ways* (l. 10485–10487) and catch-all (l. 10676) bend it as well. Before round 6 the aqueduct added an arch to the curtain's run, so a refusal on a locked wall had a reason. Now it has none, yet the row's words still refuse the aqueduct, and the new exemption, by naming only the beneath direction, invites that reading. The case is common: every drawn wall is 'locked by default' (§7.2 *Drawn constraints*, l. 10820; 'a drawn feature is locked besides', l. 10812). A user who draws a wall with T3 and then an aqueduct across it with T4 gets `refuse.locked` from one builder and `bend.wall.aqueductArch` from another. The crossing table has no column for a locked wall (C8 is the raised way held), and T110-2 (1)'s hand aqueduct crosses a generated, unlocked ring, so no bar decides it. The same literal reading refuses a raised deck drawn over a locked ground way, which §7.4's raised-way row (l. 11447) allows ('a raised way over a locked way keeps its span `open`').
issues.required_change: §7.1's lock row, cause: '— a drawn way across a locked entity (never a ground way, a carve or a wall stretch passing beneath a locked or pinned raised way's deck, which changes none of its parts: §2.7's crossing and way-and-channel tables, bent by the rows below as beneath an unlocked one),' → '— a drawn way across a locked entity (never a ground way, a carve or a wall stretch passing beneath a locked or pinned raised way's deck, nor a raised way's deck passing over a locked or pinned ground way or an aqueduct's span passing over a locked or pinned wall's band, none of which changes any part of what it passes: §2.7's crossing and way-and-channel tables, *over the band*; §7.4's raised-way row — each bent by the rows below as with an unlocked one),'. Second end, scope, §13.2 T110-2 (1): after 'and a hand aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, its course bent clear of a tower, with `bend.wall.aqueductArch`' add '— and the same across a wall drawn by hand (locked by its drawing, §7.2) and across one the user locked, no `refuse.locked`, nothing of the wall written'.

issues.claim: §5.4's `warnings` comment (l. 9332, round 6's (D3)) lists 'S5a's and S7's `W_RAISED_CROSSING` (one per crossing of a trace laid after a raised way with its deck line and per channel stopped at its under-deck strip …)' without saying which stage counts which, and the producers' texts do not settle it. (a) §4.8's lead (l. 7692) has S7 report 'each crossing of a trace laid after it with its deck line', while §4.4 S5a *Outer moats* (l. 5989) reads 'the trace meeting it by §2.7's crossing table (*beneath*) and the channel by its way-and-channel table (row e), reported (`W_RAISED_CROSSING`)'. A builder following both counts a stage-2 trace's crossing twice, against the crossing table's 'once per crossing' (l. 2655–2659). (b) The way-and-channel table's row (e) (l. 2586) also reports a stopped 'moat (S3 (10)'s …)' or canal, which meets a raised way at a regeneration under a held one (W3; T110-2 (6)'s New random on the moated c15 fixture). §4.2 S3 (10) carves it with no raised-way text, and §5.4 names no S3 count. repair-r6-determinism filed this as a hand-off, and it has not landed. (c) No bar reads the generation count of trace crossings: T110-2 (3) names `W_RAISED_CROSSING` only for the stopped channel, while T-V6-47 counts the epoch's crossings. What is built and its geometry do not change; only the report's bookkeeping does.
